turns.doctor_question: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?
turns.patient_response: Well, doctor, I came in because... I just keep steering clear of my own workshop out back. And, honestly, any family get-together where my brother-in-law might show up. It's been going on a while, and I'm just tired of planning my whole life around not running into those reminders.

symptom_reasoning.S070: The patient explicitly states they avoid their workshop and family gatherings to prevent running into reminders, demonstrating external avoidance of trauma-related stimuli.

turns.doctor_question: Can you tell me more about why you avoid your workshop and family gatherings where your brother-in-law might be? What exactly are you worried might happen if you were to go there?
turns.patient_response:
Well, it's not exactly that I'm worried something new is going to happen. It's more about what it brings up. 

If I go out to the shop, or if I have to look at him, it just... well, out of nowhere I'll see his hand with that heavy tool again. It's like a picture that just pops right into my head. It even happens when I'm nowhere near him, just going about my day, like when I'm shaving in the morning or working on a painting. And whenever that picture pops up, it still makes my chest tighten. I just stay away from him and the shop because I don't want to trigger those images.

symptom_reasoning.S069: The patient describes intrusive mental images of a heavy tool popping into their head out of nowhere and causing chest tightness, reflecting recurrent intrusive traumatic memories and physiological reactivity.
